_what: Wind climatology at SBGR, for choosing the departure runway. NOT an on-field anemometer record, and NOT the ATC flow log - GRU is an ATC-assigned flow and the tower, not the wind alone, picks the configuration. The wind says which flow is AVAILABLE most often.

_source.dataset: ERA5 reanalysis, hourly 10 m wind, via the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API
_source.grid_point_used: lat -23.44464 lon -46.46689, elevation 744 m (the API's nearest cell - on the field)
_source.licence: ERA5: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) / ECMWF, free use with attribution. Open-Meteo API data: CC BY 4.0.
_source.caveat: ERA5 is a ~25 km reanalysis. Reliable for prevailing direction and flow fractions; not for gusts or single days.

summary.verdict: East flow (RWY 10L/10R) is available ~2/3 of all hours and ~78% of morning hours; the sea-breeze/NW turn makes early-to-mid afternoon (12-15 local) the one window where west flow (28s) is the more likely configuration. Crosswind is a non-issue - the runways lie along the prevailing ESE-NW axis. With a 5 kt tailwind allowance either flow is flyable 87-94% of the time, which is why ATC demand, not wind, usually decides.
